audit_note: Audited 2026-11-23: FAIL. This run was reported as a pass of the official t14 check (move the mouse onto the pad, then click the left button). The audit found the move was not a controlled push. The arm's reference for that segment sat about 28 m below the table, so the arm could not track it: it ran in IK recovery (the controller's fallback when a target cannot be solved) for the whole segment, about 28.5 m off its reference, and collapsed onto the desk. Only the arm's wrist link ever touched the mouse; no palm or finger did. It had already knocked the mouse 69 mm before the first tick, and it then dragged it sideways to 232 mm, 43° off the commanded direction, pressing the right button at the start. The push missed its own target by 687 mm and the run's own result records push_ok = false. The scene is a rebuilt arena with no pad on the table, so the mouse was never moved onto a pad; the 'official' check filled in the on-pad, right-button and early-click terms with passing values. What stands: the left click. In the recorded run the audit found three presses of the left button, timed with the commanded press strokes, peaking at 14.5 mm; this re-run's click read 15.5 mm. A click alone is not the task.

audit.finding: Not a pass of move-and-click: the arm's reference sat 28 m below the table, so the arm collapsed onto the desk and its wrist link knocked and dragged the mouse 232 mm (further from where the pad belongs) while pressing the right button, in a rebuilt arena with no pad on the table; the 'official' check assumed the pad, right-button and early-click terms, and only the final left click (14.5 mm, commanded) is real.
